notice: SIMULATED. Fictional personas for a pre-test; not real people and not real participants. See docs/simulated_evaluation.md.

caregivers.persona: Wanjiru, 24, first-time mother in Nairobi. Secondary education. Uses a smartphone every day (WhatsApp, M-Pesa, TikTok). Has never used a parenting app. Comfortable reading English.
Otieno, 31, father and primary-school teacher in Kisumu. Very comfortable with phones; has used a baby-tracking app before. Reads English fluently.

Mama Njeri, 58, grandmother looking after her grandchild in Murang'a. Kikuyu is her first language; reads English slowly. Uses an Android phone mainly for calls, M-Pesa and WhatsApp voice notes. Prefers large text. Chose the scenario card.
Achieng, 27, bank clerk in Nairobi, expecting her first baby in about 3 months. Confident with apps (banking, shopping). Reads English fluently.
Fatuma, 35, mother of three in Mombasa. Swahili is her first language; reads English well enough for everyday use. Uses a mid-range smartphone for WhatsApp, Facebook and M-Pesa.
Kevin, 29, software tester in Nairobi, father of an 8-month-old. Very confident with apps and quick to notice rough edges.
Mercy, 20, young mother in Nakuru with a 3-month-old. Buys small data bundles. Uses Instagram and WhatsApp daily on an older phone. Comfortable reading English.
Joyce, 40, day-care worker in Thika looking after a 30-month-old in her care. Uses a smartphone for M-Pesa and WhatsApp groups. Reads English comfortably but is not used to apps beyond those.

readers.persona: Mother, 28, sales assistant in Nairobi, one 2-year-old. Reads quickly, answers briefly.
Grandfather, 63, retired teacher in Nyeri, helps with a grandchild. Careful reader, gives full answers.
University student, 21, no children. Skims and paraphrases the aim rather than the reason.
Nanny, 33, Swahili first language, looks after a 1-year-old. Short, plain answers; unsure of words like 'sensory'.
Father, 24, motorbike taxi rider in Kisumu, 6-month-old at home. Very short answers.
Mother, 30, accountant in Nairobi, 18-month-old. Precise, notices numbers.
Aunt, 45, market trader in Eldoret, often minds her sister's toddler. Answers in practical terms.
Mother, 26, hairdresser in Nakuru, 4-month-old. Anxious about her baby's development.
Father, 38, pastor in Machakos, three children, youngest 2. Reflective answers.
Mother, 29, primary-school teacher in Kiambu, 10-month-old. Confident reader.
